title: What If a Whale Died on the Seafloor? It Feeds the Deep for 50 Years

scenes.text: What if a whale died on the seafloor? It becomes a feast lasting decades.
First, sleeper sharks, hagfish and crabs strip the flesh. That stage lasts up to two years.
Then bone-eating worms move in. Some stay on a single carcass for up to ten years.
Next, bacteria break down the fats inside the bones and release hydrogen sulphide, which feeds clams and tube worms.
One whale filmed off Vancouver Island, 1,288 meters down, was still feeding this community after about 20 years.
In the end, one body can feed life in the dark for up to 50 years, in a place with almost no food.

description:
What if a whale died on the seafloor?
Its body feeds scavengers, bone-eating worms and bacteria-fed clams for up to 50 years.
